item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
A classic and one of my favourites! I just love the fact that it's a genuinely nice SCP for a change, plus the interaction with 173 is great (and one of the main reasons why I think people shouldn't be so wary of articles that refer to other SCPs.

The only nitpick I have is that even if they're harmless, I don't see the Foundation allowing a non-humanoid SCP to just walk around a facility freely (and even then it's rare for them allow humanoid ones this privilege). Maybe if they were restrained to a "safe" area, but to allow them in Euclid and Keter areas seems a bit much as that seems like a big potential containment breach hazard.

It's especially surprising considering if I remember correctly, this article was written at a time when the SCP Foundation was shown to be far more ruthless and evil (pretty sure we still had that silly "mandatory monthly termination" thing going back in the days).

item.content:encoded: I don't like this one. First off, the tone is quite poor, but I guess it's understandable as this was written back in the early days of the Foundation. The main aspect responsible for my downvote is the fact that they are given free roam of the facility. But they're so cute and wuvvable! Yeah, and SCP-1048 was, too, before it started creating duplicates of itself and singlehandedly razed a site and slaughtered all the MTFs sent to contain it. The point is that even if an object seems to be benign, its behaivor could change at anytime, and the Foundation would never risk that occuring (at least, after the 1048 incident). Couple the fact that we're entrusting the containment of a Euclid-class object to these guys, and my downvote is sealed. Seriously, why are we trusting these things?

I kinda like these, but they have a problem I've seen elsewhere: trust. item.content:encoded: I want one

I'm a bit of a math nerd (not quite as much as my brother who has a degree in math, but still), hence the excitedness of my upvote making a square of a prime. Woo! =P

Anyway, I like there being weird little things like this that aren't murder machines or something. Not everything anamolous has to be super creepy, evil, or deadly. I like to think there would be at least a few things that are similar to these, just being unassuming and wonky.

I do feel the need to repeat the previous comments regarding putting some sort of tracking devices on them. I don't get why someone has to physically locate them every hour. Especially with the "lost in the vents" thing happening multiple times, tracking devices would likely save a lot of hassle in the long run. Even if it mentions it was tried, but they always managed to shake the devices off or something. Not even trying it seems… odd, to say the least.
